rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An initial alif marks the later action as more severe or weighty in existence than the action preceding it, as slaughter exceeds punishment and advancing corruption exceeds added harm.
rows.anchor: زيدت الألف تنبيها على أن المؤخر أشد فى الوجود من المقدم عليه لفظا

rows.speaker: من رأى
rows.claim: One view writes the disputed alif because return to Hell and being gathered to God are more severe than worldly torment or death.
rows.anchor: فمن رأى أن مرجعهم إلى الجحيم أشد من أكل الزقوم وشرب الحميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi prefers omitting the disputed alif: the matters are unseen, so the two conditions are not equally known to us.
rows.anchor: ومن لم ير ذلك لأنه غيب عنا فلم يستو القسمان فى العلم بهما لم يثبته وهو أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif in these forms signals that despair follows patience and waiting for relief, which are easier states.
rows.anchor: لأن الصبر وانتظار الفرج أخف من الإياس والإياس لا يكون فى الوجود إلا بعد الصبر والانتظار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An added alif after plural waw marks the weight of the verbal clause; it remains when a subjunctive or jussive governs the verb, as here.
rows.anchor: فإن دخل ناصب أو جازم مثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif is omitted in some places to signal an action's lack of real existence, as futile striving in falsehood cannot endure.
rows.anchor: وقد تسقط مواضع للتنبيه على اضمحلال الفعل نحو

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A reported distinction is that لا يتمنونه follows a condition applying at any time, while لن يتمنوه answers a demand to wish for death now; the latter is compared with لن تراني.
rows.anchor: ووجه القول الثاني ان ﴿ ولا يتمنونه ﴾ جاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi concludes that لا and لن simply negate future actions; whether negation is eternal comes from external evidence, not from either particle itself.
rows.anchor: والحق ان لا ولن لمجرد النفي عن الافعال المستقبله والتأبيد وعدمه يؤخذان من دليل خارج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Claims that لن inherently means perpetual negation fail because the Qur'an limits it by today, adds أبدا after it, and gives it an endpoint in other passages.
rows.anchor: ولو كانت للتأبيد لم يقيد منفيها باليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Perpetual negation can be expressed with لا as well, so eternal force does not belong uniquely to لن.
rows.anchor: وقد استعملت لا للاستغراق الابدي فى قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An adjective restricts an indefinite noun but clarifies a definite one; divine attributes in the basmala praise God rather than distinguish Him from another.
rows.anchor: وهي مخصصة ان وقعت صفة للنكرة وموضحة للمعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attributes in the basmala serve praise, not identification; Abu al-Tayyib's verse likewise says names of a praised person added no new knowledge.
rows.anchor: فليس ذكر الوصف هنا للتمييز لأنه ليس له مثل تعالى الله عن ذلك

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi takes the calf passages to omit a second object: they took the calf as a deity; otherwise merely making a calf would warrant divine anger.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي فأما قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi objects that the Israelites worshipped the calf, so the construction can mean they took the calf and worshipped it as a deity.
rows.anchor: لأن الواقع أن اولئك عبدوه فالتقدير على هذا فى المتعدي لواحد

rows.speaker: أثير الدين
rows.claim: Athir al-Din allows اتخذ to take one object with an understood clause, preferring this because a two-object construction would state its second object somewhere.
rows.anchor: ولهذا جوز الشيخ أثير الدين فى هذه الآيات كلها أن تكون اتخذ فيها متعدية إلى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sometimes a transitive verb is treated as intransitive because only the occurrence of the action matters; no omitted object is intended, and such an object is termed dead.
rows.anchor: ألا يكون المفعول مقصودا أصلا وينزل الفعل المتعدي منزلة القاصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not every contextually imaginable object is grammatically omitted: فعلوا, like eat and drink, can refer simply to performing the action rather than an identified object.
rows.anchor: وبهذا يعلم أنه ليس كل ما هو لازم من موضوع الكلام مقدرا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted object can be treated as nonexistent rather than elided; this differs from a generalized object, which makes affirmative wording cover more cases.
rows.anchor: ولما كان التحقيق أنه لا يعد هذا من المحذوف فإنه لا حذف فيه بالكلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A clause after علم can fill both object positions without ellipsis; in passive syntax the نائب عن الفاعل bears the agent's status and occupies the patient's position.
rows.anchor: الجملة سادة مسد المفعولين فإن الجملة محلة لاسم واحد سد مسد اسمين مفعولين من غير حذف

rows.speaker: ابن الأثير
rows.claim: Interrogatives and conditionals can compress multiple alternatives or names: كم مالك can mean twenty or thirty, and من يقم can cover Zayd or Amr; universal terms do similar work.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأثير في الجامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plural and dual forms compress repeated names; the dual contains two instances joined without an expressed conjunction, while unlike names are repeated with coordination.
rows.anchor: فإن الزيدين يغنى عن زيد وزيد وزيد وكذا التثنية أصلها رجل ورجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb فعل often stands for multiple deeds; in the challenge here, it means bringing a surah like the Qur'an, which they will never do.
rows.anchor: أي فإن لم تأتوا بسورة من مثله ولن تأتوا بسورة من مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting and delaying are eloquent techniques that display command of language and have an agreeable effect; the sound view is that they are not metaphor.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أنه ليس منه فإن المجاز نقل ما وضع له إلى ما لم يوضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كيف asks about a thing's state, unlike ما which asks about its nature and من which asks about an individual; it functions like an adverbial predicate meaning in what state.
rows.anchor: استفهام عن حال الشيء لا عن ذاته كما إن ما سؤال عن حقيقته ومن عن مشخصاته

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: كيف can be a direct question, describe a state without asking, or express astonishment; context can also give it other rhetorical forces.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم لها ثلاثة أوجه أحدها سؤال محض عن حال

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib reads كيف here as an admonitory inquiry rather than a request for unknown information; God's uses of كيف remind or rebuke the audience.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب فى تفسيره كيف هنا استخبار لا استفهام

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another account gives كيف several contextual functions: denial, rebuke, warning, prompting reflection, and confirming what precedes it; its force of denial can be followed by إلا.
rows.anchor: ولتضمنها معنى الجحد شاع إن يقع بعدها إلا

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some hold that Qur'anic meanings cannot be exhaustively classified; others leave them unclassified, as Ibn al-Sayyid reports of most Basrans in his time.
rows.anchor: زعم قوم ان معاني القرآن لا تنحصر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Speech is classified variously: as two kinds, or ten; other schemes reduce the count to nine, eight, or seven by subsuming question, intercession, or doubt under other categories.
rows.anchor: وقيل تسعة واسقطوا الاستفهام لدخوله في المسالة

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash counts six speech functions: report, inquiry, command, prohibition, call, and wish.
rows.anchor: وكان أبو الحسن الأخفش يرى أنها ستة أيضا وهي عنده الخبر والاستخبار والأمر والنهي والنداء والتمني

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A five-part scheme lists report, command, declaration, request, and call; other classifications also exist.
rows.anchor: وقيل خمسة الخبر والأمر والتصريح والطلب والنداء وقيل غير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report aims to inform its audience but can carry secondary functions such as astonishment.
rows.anchor: والقصد به إفادة المخاطب وقد يشرب مع ذلك معاني اخر

rows.speaker: ابن فارس
rows.claim: Ibn Faris defines astonishment as recognizing a thing's superiority over its peers by some quality.
rows.anchor: وهو تفضيل الشيء على أضرابه بوصف

rows.speaker: ابن الضائع
rows.claim: Ibn al-Da'i describes astonishment as an outstanding quality that sets the object apart from its peers.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الضائع استعظام صفة خرج بها المتعجب منه عن نظائره

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says astonishment magnifies an extraordinary matter in listeners' hearts because it exceeds its peers.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري في تفسير سورة الصف

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani says astonishment works through ambiguity: people wonder at causes they do not know, and obscurity strengthens the effect.
rows.anchor: وقال الرماني المطلوب فى التعجب الإبهام لأن من شأن الناس ان يتعجبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Astonishment has explicit forms ما أفعله and أفعل به, and indirect forms such as كبر and كيف in this verse.
rows.anchor: ثم قد وضعوا للتعجب صيغا من لفظه وهي ما افعله

rows.speaker: الثمانيني
rows.claim: Al-Thumani argues that astonishment forms are declarative: أسمع بهم وأبصر means how well they hear and see; God informs people that they merit others' astonishment.
rows.anchor: على انه خبر بقوله تعالى

words: إذا لذهب كل إله بما خلق
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional لو is omitted from the argument against multiple gods: if another god existed, each would take its creation and dominate the others.
rows.anchor: تقديره لو كان معه إله لذهب كل إله بما خلق

words: وما كنت تتلو من قبله من كتاب ولا تخطه بيمينك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 29:48, لو is understood: if the Prophet had read or written before revelation, the falsifiers would have doubted.
rows.anchor: معناه لو كان كذلك لارتاب المبطلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قد is understood before the past verb in واتبعك, since a past circumstantial clause normally requires قد, stated or implicit.
rows.anchor: أي وقد اتبعك لأن الماضي لا يقع موقع الحال إلا وقد معه ظاهرة أو مقدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The circumstantial clause in 2:28 likewise means وقد كنتم أمواتا, with قد omitted.
rows.anchor: لأن الماضي لا يقع موقع الحال إلا وقد معه ظاهرة أو مقدرة

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaqub's reading حصرة صدورهم supports interpreting the phrase as وقد حصرت, with قد omitted.
rows.anchor: قد حصرت بدلالة قراءة يعقوب

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash takes حصرت صدورهم as a deleted circumstantial clause or a curse that their hearts be constrained from fighting their own people.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش الحال محذوفة و حصرت

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali rejects the curse reading because they did fight their people; the apt prayer would be that God set their forces against one another.
rows.anchor: ورده أبو علي بقوله أي قاتلوا قومهم فلا يجوز أن يدعى عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction means أن يريكم البرق, with أن omitted.
rows.anchor: ومنه حذف أن فى قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لا is omitted from تفتأ because the verb means to continue and is conventionally negated: لا تفتأ.
rows.anchor: أي لا تفتأ لأنها ملازمة للنفي ومعناها لا تبرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means أن لا تميد بكم, with لا omitted.
rows.anchor: وألقى فى الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is interpreted as أن لا تبوء بإثمي وإثمك, with لا omitted.
rows.anchor: إني أريد أن تبوء بإثمي وإثمك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation resolves the difficulty by taking the verse to mean those who cannot endure fasting; لا is understood before يطيقونه.
rows.anchor: وبهذا يزول الإشكال من الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an often deletes a preposition and attaches the verb directly to its object: اختيار موسى قومه means he chose from his people, and similar examples follow.
rows.anchor: كثر فى القرآن حذف الجار ثم إيصال الفعل إلى المجرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concordance notes أمواتا in the accusative in Baqarah, Ali Imran, and al-Mursalat, alongside comparable formula and spelling variations across surahs.
rows.anchor: ﴿ أمواتا ﴾ بالنصب فى البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inventory records where parallel Qur'anic phrases include or omit letters and vary in form, including this opening with waw in Baqarah, al-Hijr, and Sad.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وإذ قال ربك للملائكة ﴾ بواو فى البقرة والحجر وص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other listed parallels include ونزلنا in three surahs versus وأنزلنا elsewhere, فإن توليتم in three, ألم يروا without waw in three, and specified forms of أجل, تراب, and إرسال الرسل.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ونزلنا ﴾ ثلاثة أحرف فى طه والنحل وق

words: لا يسمعون فيها لغوا ولا تأثيما
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the pairing, لغو is the first, lower stage of objectionable speech and تأثيم its further stage; censure presupposes an offense and a belief that it is blameworthy.
rows.anchor: اللغو منشأ المنكر ومبدأ درجاته والتأثيم منشأ التكبر ومبدأ درجاته

words: أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels' wording pairs corruption with glorification and bloodshed with sanctification: glorification supports reform, while sanctification protects blood; the latter is nobler.
rows.anchor: فقابل الإفساد بالتسبيح والحمد وسفك الدماء بالتقديس

words: يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four terms form earthly and heavenly pairs, with the soul positioned between them; corruption and sanctification are the far ends, and the middle terms bridge earth and heaven.
rows.anchor: وهذا شكل مربع من أرضى وهو الإفساد وسفك الدماء وسمائي وهو التسبيح والتقديس

words: أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها ويسفك الدماء ونحن نسبح بحمدك ونقدس لك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashi calls this analysis profound and says it opens further insights into Qur'anic passages, including the Throne Verse.
rows.anchor: وهذا القدر الذي ذكره هذا الحبر مرمى عظيم يوصل إلى أمور غير متجاسر عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One type of مقابلة pairs each earlier item immediately with its counterpart, as night is paired with day.
rows.anchor: أحدها أن يأتي بكل واحد من المقدمات مع قرينة من الثواني

words: جعل لكم الليل والنهار لتسكنوا فيه ولتبتغوا من فضله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second type presents all the earlier items first, then their counterparts in matching order; examples include the night and day and the stages of apostasy and punishment.
rows.anchor: والثانية أن يأتي بجميع الثواني مرتبة من أولها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Raising فنخرج establishes the greening; making it subjunctive would reverse the point and imply failure to give thanks, as Zamakhshari explains.
rows.anchor: الرابع أنه لو نصب لأعطى ما هو عكس الغرض لأن معناه إثبات الاخضرار

rows.speaker: ابن الخباز
rows.claim: Ibn al-Khabaz says the subjunctive would spoil the meaning: seeing the water is not what causes greening; the water itself does.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الخباز النصب يفسد المعنى لأن رؤية المخاطب الماء الذي أنزله الله ليس سببا للاخضرار

words: نسوق الماء إلى الأرض الجرز فنخرج به زرعا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present verb فتثير among past verbs makes the wind's cloud-raising vivid and certain to the listener.
rows.anchor: ﴿ والله الذي أرسل الرياح فتثير سحابا فسقناه إلى بلد ميت ﴾

words: نسوق الماء إلى الأرض الجرز فنخرج به زرعا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although reviving earth matters, stirring clouds is more astonishing because its cause is hidden; people recognize water's effect on crops more readily than wind's role in rain.
rows.anchor: وإثارة السحاب أعجبها فكان أولى بالتخصيص بالمضارع وإنما قال إن إثارة السحاب أعجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passive participle can replace a future verb and carry a past sense, presenting the gathering as settled and encompassing everyone; compare يوم يجمعكم ليوم الجمع.
rows.anchor: ﴿ يوم مجموع له الناس ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ma'idah completes the legal ordinances and religion: it gathers prohibitions and permissions, protection of life, property, intellect and faith, and laws distinctive to Muhammad's community.
rows.anchor: وأما المائدة فسورة العقود وبهن تمام الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ottoman order of Baqarah, Ali Imran, al-Nisa, then al-Ma'idah is especially well arranged; Ibn Masud's codex put al-Nisa before Ali Imran, and surah order was chosen by scholarly judgment, not divinely prescribed.
rows.anchor: وهذا الترتيب بين هذه السور الأربع المدنيات البقرة وآل عمران والنساء والمائدة من أحسن الترتيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an was not collected as a codex during the Prophet's life while revelation continued; Abu Bakr and the Companions compiled it after his death, then Uthman copied and dispatched codices.
rows.anchor: فلهذا تأخرت كتابته إلى أن كمل نزول القرآن بموته صلى الله عليه وسلم فكتب أبو بكر والصحابة بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Order can reflect what matters to the addressee: answer a greeting with better or equal words, and place relatives first among recipients of charity.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فحيوا بأحسن منها أو ردوها ﴾

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi explains that expiation precedes blood money for killing a Muslim because a Muslim puts God's right before his own, while a non-Muslim prioritizes himself.
rows.anchor: أن المسلم يرى تقديم حق الله على نفسه

words: فدية مسلمة إلى أهله وتحرير رقبة مؤمنة
rows.speaker: ابن أبي هريرة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hurayra says the changed order for a treaty-protected victim avoids wrongly extending that ruling to a believing victim killed among enemy people.
rows.anchor: إنما خالف بينهما ولم يجعلهما على نسق واحد

rows.speaker: نجم الدين بن الرفعة
rows.claim: Ibn al-Rif'a offers another rationale: blood money highlights the surprising protection secured by treaty for an otherwise unprotected life, while expiation is more striking for a protected Muslim killed by mistake.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يقال إنه لما كان الكفر يهدر الدماء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Dhu al-Qarnayn's westward journey is mentioned before his eastward one to focus attention, perhaps because western people were then more rebellious; another reason may be unknown.
rows.anchor: قيل لماذا بدأ بالمغرب قبل المشرق وكان مسكن ذي القرنين من ناحية المشرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Delaying the person praised or blamed can emphasize the intended focus: نعم الرجل زيد is stronger than placing Zayd first.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا أن تأخر المقصود بالمدح والذم أولى من تقدمه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: A preceding, context-truncated report from Qatada identifies the referents as angels; al-Zarkashi says the antecedent already mentioned fits better.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن قتادة قال هم الملائكة والأشبه أن يأتي هنا بما سبق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One parsing makes أحق predicate of God and His Messenger; its singular form is used, and pleasing God also pleases His Messenger.
rows.anchor: فقيل أحق خبر عنهما وسهل إفراد الضمير بعدم إفراد أحق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another parsing makes أحق refer to the Prophet, with the predicate of God omitted because the second is understood from it.
rows.anchor: وقيل أحق خبر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وحذف من الأول لدلالة الثاني عليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third account reverses the omission; the singular pronoun avoids joining God and His Messenger under one pronoun, and al-Zamakhshari reads the Messenger as the intended object of pleasing.
rows.anchor: وقيل العكس وإنما أفرد الضمير لئلا يجمع بين اسم الله ورسوله فى ضمير واحد

words: أطيعوا الله ورسوله ولا تولوا عنه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular pronoun in ولا تولوا عنه is another example of referring to the Messenger after mentioning God and His Messenger together.
rows.anchor: ومنها قوله تعالى ﴿ يا أيها الذين آمنوا أطيعوا الله ورسوله ولا تولوا عنه ﴾

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The pronoun إنّها may refer to prayer as the nearer noun, to the understood act of seeking help, or to both with the first term omitted.
rows.anchor: فقيل الضمير للصلاة لأنها أقرب المذكورين وقيل أعاده على المعنى وهو الاستعانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the Friday passage the pronoun returns to trade despite its distance and feminine form, because trade attracts more than amusement, is more useful, or was primary while the drum-led entertainment was secondary.
rows.anchor: أعاده فى آية الجمعة على التجارة وإن كانت أبعد ومؤنثة أيضا لأنها أجذب للقلوب

rows.speaker: البخاري
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari's report says a caravan arrived during Friday prayer and the amusement was drum-beating to announce its arrival.
rows.anchor: كما جاء فى صحيح البخاري أقبلت عير يوم الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the phrase about casting sin upon an innocent person, the pronoun refers back to the nearer masculine إثم.
rows.anchor: على الإثم رعاية لمرتبة القرب والتذكير
